responsibility: This module is GCC’s target backend for the CRIS architecture family, covering both generic CRIS code generation and its ELF and GNU/Linux subtargets. It supplies the target description, option handling, and executable backend hooks that connect generic GCC RTL expansion and final emission to the CRIS ABI, register set, calling convention, frame layout, assembler syntax, and runtime environment. Its machine-description files define CRIS instruction selection, operand predicates and constraints, condition-code modes, delay-slot and compare handling, addressing-mode exploitation, and atomic/synchronization sequences, while the main target source and headers implement costs, legality checks, prologue/epilogue and varargs logic, trampoline and thunk support, asm printing, tuning, and target-specific RTL pass integration. The accompanying option and subtarget files specialize this behavior for architecture variants and Linux/ELF linkage conventions, making this module the locus for all CRIS-specific low-level code generation and assembly interface behavior.
